sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Origin**: Derived from the Mongol decimal system (Chengiz Khan), adapted to Indian conditions. 
• **Dual Rank**: Every Mansabdar held two ranks: **Zat** (personal rank/status/salary) and **Sawar** (number of cavalrymen to be maintained). 
• **Nature**: It was not hereditary; the Emperor could promote, demote, or dismiss a Mansabdar at will. 
• **Payment**: Salaries were paid either in cash (**Naqd**) or through land grants (**Jagir**). Those paid via Jagir were called **Jagirdars**.

Prelims: Crucial for understanding the 'Do-aspa Sih-aspa' evolution.

items.definition: System of branding horses (Dagh) and descriptive rolls of soldiers (Chehra) introduced to prevent corruption and ensure the quality of the cavalry.
Introduced by Jahangir; allowed a Mansabdar to maintain double or triple the number of horses without increasing the Zat rank.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Centralization**: Eliminated the middleman (local chiefs) by bringing officials directly under the Emperor. 
• **Bureaucratic Integration**: Combined civil and military functions into a single hierarchy.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Jagirdari Crisis**: Over-assignment of Jagirs leading to 'Be-jagiri' (shortage of land) in the late Mughal period. 
• **Corruption**: Difficulty in maintaining the exact number of horses during long campaigns.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'ZS-DC' (Zat-Sawar, Dagh-Chehra). 
• **Decoded Meaning**: ZS = The Rank (Zat/Sawar), DC = The Control (Dagh/Chehra).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: Mansabdars were NOT necessarily military commanders; many were civil officials. The system was a 'bureaucratic' system, not just a 'military' one.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Bureaucratic-Military Complex' to describe the Mansabdari system in answers regarding Mughal state formation.

keyTakeaways: The Mansabdari system was a non-hereditary, graded hierarchy.
Zat determined status/pay; Sawar determined military obligation.
Dagh and Chehra were essential anti-corruption mechanisms.
